name: HGH + insulin pairing

card.summary: HGH plus insulin pairing is a bodybuilding practice in which growth hormone and insulin are used together in the belief that the combination builds more muscle and a fuller, leaner physique.
card.note: Insulin misuse can cause severe hypoglycemia, coma and death, and GH is a prescription-only drug with an illegal off-label distribution market in the US.

quick.overview:
HGH plus insulin pairing is a combination used in some bodybuilding circles. Practitioners believe growth hormone supports lean mass and fat loss while insulin, an anabolic hormone, drives nutrients into muscle, so together they are meant to produce a bigger, fuller, leaner physique.

Research on the specific combination in healthy lifters is minimal. Wikipedia notes that evidence for insulin's muscle-building effect is limited to a small group of drug-naive individuals, and that it is unclear whether insulin improves athletic performance. Reviews and clinical literature emphasise that GH induces insulin resistance and that insulin carries a risk of dangerous hypoglycemia.
quick.how: In bodybuilding culture the pairing is described as an advanced, high-risk strategy used mainly by competitive and enhanced athletes, typically alongside other performance-enhancing drugs and tightly controlled meals. Both hormones are obtained outside normal medical channels in most such cases. Details of amounts, timing and administration are not given here.
quick.risks: The central documented danger is hypoglycemia (low blood sugar), which can progress to seizures, coma, brain damage and death. GH can raise insulin resistance and diabetes risk, and prolonged excess GH produces acromegaly features such as thickened jaw, hands and feet. Insulin abuse has been mentioned as a possible factor in the deaths of bodybuilders. GH is prescription-only, and the IOC has banned insulin for non-diabetic athletes since 1998.

lead: HGH plus insulin pairing refers to the use of human growth hormone (GH) together with insulin in bodybuilding. People who use it say the combination improves muscle fullness, recovery and leanness: GH is associated with lean-mass gains and fat reduction, and insulin with nutrient uptake and reduced protein breakdown. It is generally discussed as an advanced practice among enhanced competitors, and sites that document drug use in bodybuilding classify it as high risk.

Insulin was first raised as a possible athletic aid around 1998, when the IOC banned its use by non-diabetic athletes [1]. Bodybuilders are reported to use it, often with growth hormone, in the belief that it builds muscle; proposed mechanisms include increased protein synthesis and reduced protein breakdown, but the evidence base is limited to a small group of drug-naive people [1]. Whether insulin improves athletic performance is described as unclear [1].

Growth hormone itself has been used by athletes since at least 1982, and sporting bodies including the IOC and NCAA ban it [2]. A 2007 Stanford meta-analysis in older adults found about 2 kg more lean mass and a similar fat decrease but no strength gains, and the added lean mass may reflect water retention [2].

chain: GH used for lean-mass and fat-loss effects
Insulin used to shuttle nutrients into muscle
angle.text: Bodybuilders use the pairing to try to enlarge muscle and sharpen conditioning. The claimed effects are those of the two hormones; the combination has not been established by trials in healthy lifters, and it carries serious safety risks.

infobox: Both are prescription drugs; insulin is banned for non-diabetic athletes by the IOC (1998)
Distributing HGH for non-recognised uses is a felony under a 1990 law

paras: The pairing combines two hormones that act on metabolism in opposing ways. GH induces insulin resistance and increases the risk of diabetes in patients [2], while insulin lowers blood glucose and is the main hormone driving glucose uptake. Users in bodybuilding communities combine them because they consider GH's lean-tissue and lipolytic reputation complementary to insulin's anabolic and nutrient-partitioning reputation.
Because the practice is carried out outside medical supervision, public descriptions focus on what is claimed and on the risks; no instructions are given in this article.

Insulin was first raised as a possible athletic aid around the 1998 Winter Olympics, and the IOC banned use by non-diabetic athletes in 1998 [1]. The book Game of Shadows alleged that baseball player Barry Bonds used insulin alongside other drugs [1]. A 2008 report cited on Wikipedia warned that athletes were exposing themselves to potential harm by using large amounts of growth hormone, IGF-I and insulin [1]. Insulin abuse has been mentioned as a possible factor in the deaths of bodybuilders Ghent Wakefield and Rich Piana [1].

Hypoglycemia is the main hazard of insulin and can lead to coma and death; acute risks also include brain damage and paralysis, with warning signs such as dizziness, tremors, palpitations, seizures and confusion [1].

In healthy adults, GH commonly causes injection-site reactions and less often joint swelling or pain and carpal tunnel syndrome; an immune response against GH can occur, and GH may be a risk factor for Hodgkin's lymphoma [2]. Excess GH, as in acromegaly, thickens the bones of the jaw, fingers and toes and can bring sweating, muscle weakness and insulin resistance [2]. Experimental work has linked the GH/IGF-1 axis to cancer biology [3], and a consensus statement addresses the safety of GH replacement in cancer survivors and people with pituitary tumours [4]. A case report describes acromegaly presenting with resistant acne [5].

In the US, GH is available only by prescription. The DEA has treated off-label prescribing as illegal and a major route for illicit distribution, and a 1990 law made distributing HGH for uses other than recognised medical treatment a felony [2]. The FDA has not approved GH for performance enhancement [2]. Standard urine tests do not detect GH, though blood tests that distinguish natural from artificial GH were developed in the early 2000s [2].

No studies found on the combination of GH and insulin for bodybuilding. Related research includes ClinicalTrials.gov registrations on the interplay of GH and insulin in patients with growth hormone deficiency, such as a completed study of metabolic interactions between GH and insulin in adults with GH deficiency [6], and a Phase 3 study of metabolic effects of GH and IGF-I in people with GH deficiency and diabetes or impaired glucose tolerance [7]. These involve clinical patients, not lifters.

timeline.event: Athletes have used GH to enhance performance since at least this year [2].
US law makes distributing HGH for non-recognised uses a felony [2].
The IOC bans insulin use by non-diabetic athletes [1].
Blood tests that distinguish natural from artificial GH are developed [2].
